extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting software papers to the Journal of Open Source Software (JOSS) and developers/maintainers of submission/validation templates (openbases/submission-joss)
extracted.subtask_description: Validation and automated checks for JOSS software-paper submissions using the openbases/submission-joss template and openbases-python validator; intended to catch formatting, metadata, and reproducibility issues prior to human review and official submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable word count
rubrics_metrics.description: Checking for an acceptable word count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The openbases/openbases-python validator can automatically check length (word count) to ensure the paper meets JOSS length expectations. The post notes this as an easy programmatic check but does not specify numeric limits; it's intended to catch papers that are too long/short before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validate references in paper.bib
rubrics_metrics.description: Validating the references in the paper.bib.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The validator checks the bibliography file (paper.bib) for correctness. The author points to openbases-python as the tool that performs these checks; this prevents malformed or invalid reference entries from reaching the submission stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generate PDF preview
rubrics_metrics.description: Generating a PDF to preview (before you submit!).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The submission-joss template and openbases/openbases-pdf container can build a PDF preview locally or via CI. A rendered preview is made available as a build artifact or live paper, letting authors inspect how the paper will appear before official submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check for an open source license
rubrics_metrics.description: Checking for an open source license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The validator checks that the repository includes an open source license so that the code accompanying the JOSS paper is properly licensed. This is part of ensuring the submission meets JOSS's expectations around openness and reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check for CONTRIBUTING.md
rubrics_metrics.description: Checking for a CONTRIBUTING.md file in the repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of CONTRIBUTING.md is verified so that projects provide contributor guidance. This is a standard repository hygiene check performed by the template/validator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markdown and bibliography validation
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper markdown and bibliography are tested and validated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond individual checks, the template runs validation on the paper.md and paper.bib to ensure they conform to expected formatting and structure. The post emphasizes that these automated checks catch many easy/structural errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check formatting (length and formatting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Checking for correct formatting of the paper (including length and formatting conventions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author states the validator checks 'easy things like length and formatting.' This encompasses structural/formatting rules (e.g., expected markdown structure) that can be enforced automatically prior to human review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metadata extraction from markdown
rubrics_metrics.description: Extracting and validating metadata from the paper markdown file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The openbases tools extract metadata values from paper.md (e.g., fields needed for rendering and indexing). The validator ensures required metadata is present and usable for building the paper and generating badges/icons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous integration and build artifacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Connect the repository to CI (e.g., CircleCI) and Github Pages to run validation/builds and produce artifacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recommended workflow is to fork the template, add your paper, and connect to CircleCI/GitHub Pages. CI runs the validators, builds the PDF/HTML preview, and exposes rendered previews as build artifacts or live pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archive previews/versioned artifacts per commit
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate and archive outputs (e.g., PDF) named by commit for each build.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The template creates an archive named by commit for each generated PDF so intermediate versions are preserved. This supports reproducibility and a 'living publication' model where the paper and code evolve over time without losing history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility: code and paper under version control
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the entire generation of the paper and testing of the software is documented and under version control to support reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post emphasizes JOSS's strength in reproducibility: the paper generation, tests, and code are all in version control and produce a DOI. Validators and CI help make submissions reproducible by capturing the exact commit and build artifacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tool limitation: does not replace human content review
rubrics_metrics.description: Automated validation will not check the human components of the submission — reading the text of the paper and evaluating quality/content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author explicitly warns that submission-joss and the validators are for structural/technical checks only and will not replace the human-driven review process (Whedon/JOSS reviewers) that assesses scientific quality, writing quality, and substantive content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with JOSS checklist/process
rubrics_metrics.description: Conform to JOSS's openly-stated submission process and checklist (the process is clearly stated with checklists and easy back-and-forth review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post notes that JOSS uses a transparent checklist-driven review process; the template/validator aims to automate the 'easy' checklist items so human reviewers can focus on substantive review. Authors should follow JOSS checklist items not covered by automation.
